title: Loading a LoRA right
hook: LoraLoader or LoraLoaderModelOnly, two strengths, chains, and the one log line that tells you the file didn't fit your model.

verified.claim: A key nobody claims logs 'lora key not loaded: <key>'. We ran the real load_lora with a small fake file and saw these lines, and it patched only the matching layer.
LoraLoaderModelOnly calls load_lora_for_models with clip None, so no text-encoder keys are in the key map.
If both strengths are 0, LoraLoader returns its inputs unchanged.
A patched key that the model lacks logs NOT LOADED.
A file with no alpha gets scale 1 whatever its rank.
A shape mismatch logs ERROR with the adapter name and key, and leaves the weight unchanged.

unchecked: No real LoRA or checkpoint ran for this lesson. Which layer names a real file uses, and how its text-encoder part affects a picture, was not tested.
Strength advice (start at 1, try 0.5 to 1) is common practice, not measured here.
